title: no v3 equivalent of intent claude upgrade --skip-settings
body:
v2 had `intent claude upgrade --skip-settings`, which declined `.claude/settings.json` and the hook scripts. v3 has no equivalent: `intent claude upgrade --help` lists `--apply` and `--force` only. A project that does not want Claude Code lifecycle hooks wired has no way to say so, and the previous version had one.

MEASURED, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. `intent claude upgrade --skip-settings` and `intent upgrade --skip-settings` both exit 1 with `error: unexpected argument`; `intent claude upgrade` alone exits 0. The v2 flag is real and still on disk at `intent/plugins/claude/bin/intent_claude_upgrade` lines 74, 93, 118, 674 and 856-860, where it gates both the settings block and the hook scripts as a single escape hatch.

FOUND BY laksa-vc DRIVING A FRESH INSTALL FROM OUTSIDE THE ESTATE, not by anyone inside it. They were tracing which verb creates `.claude/` for an unrelated reason and read the shipped CLAUDE.md paragraph that documents the flag.

THE DOC HALF IS FIXED AND WAS WRONG ON THREE AXES AT ONCE, WHICH IS WHY IT SURVIVED. `lib/templates/llm/_CLAUDE.md` said `.claude/settings.json` is installed "the default, declined by `intent upgrade --skip-settings`". Three false claims in one sentence: it is not the default; `intent upgrade` does not install it at all (the verb is `intent claude upgrade --apply`); and the flag does not exist on either verb in v3. The wrong-verb half was ALREADY WRONG IN v2 -- `grep -c skip-settings bin/intent_upgrade` returns 0 against a positive control of 27 for `upgrade` in the same file, so the flag was only ever on `intent claude upgrade`. A sentence carrying a pre-existing error plus a port-time regression reads exactly like a sentence that is merely stale.

WHY IT MATTERED MORE THAN A TYPO. That paragraph is the one telling a reader how the session-hook mechanism is installed and how to decline it. It is in a GENERATED file, so no project could fix it locally without the fix being overwritten, and it shipped to every Intent project. A reader wanting to decline had no working instruction; a reader diagnosing absent hooks was pointed at the wrong verb.

THE QUESTION THIS ISSUE IS ACTUALLY FOR: was dropping the flag deliberate? Under fail-forward, removing a v2 flag is legitimate when it is a decision. Nothing found so far records this one as a decision rather than an omission at port time, and the doc continuing to advertise it is weak evidence for omission. If deliberate, this closes with the reason recorded. If not, the flag is owed -- it is the only escape hatch for a project that wants Intent without Claude Code lifecycle hooks.

Driven by vc. Found by laksa-vc. Doc half fixed in the template and propagated.
